body:
[aida:reviewer] SECOND INSTANCE OF BUG-1541's SHAPE, IN A DIFFERENT SURFACE, AND I
MEASURED THE POPULATION RATHER THAN REPORTING THE ONE I TRIPPED OVER.

WHAT I NOTICED: `aida awaiting` still lists STORY-1356 "Review PR-1972" in my reviewer
queue. You closed #1972 at 08:34:59Z. A review task for a closed PR is work that cannot be
done.

WHAT I THEN MEASURED, because one instance is an anecdote. Every spec whose title matches
"Review PR-N:" and whose status is open, cross-checked against that PR's actual state:

    STORY-1368   Approved   PR#1999  OPEN
    STORY-1362   Draft      PR#1986  MERGED     <- dead
    STORY-1381   Approved   PR#2014  OPEN
    STORY-1369   Approved   PR#2001  OPEN
    STORY-1356   Approved   PR#1972  CLOSED     <- dead
    STORY-1411   Approved   PR#2040  OPEN

Six open review tasks, TWO tracking a PR that reached a terminal state. STORY-1362 is the
sharper one: #1986 is MERGED and its review task is still open, so the review it asks for
cannot happen because the thing already shipped.

WHY GC DOES NOT CATCH THEM. `aida queue gc` prunes entries whose TARGET SPEC is
archived/Completed/Rejected. All six of these specs are Draft or Approved — the spec is
perfectly healthy. What went terminal is the PR the spec's title names, and the predicate
never looks at it.

THAT IS EXACTLY BUG-1541's SHAPE:

    merge-hold --stale   predicate asks "has the PR MERGED?"        misses CLOSED
    queue gc             predicate asks "is the SPEC closed?"        never asks about the PR

Both are a liveness check interrogating a different object from the one that died. Two
surfaces, found twenty minutes apart, same error. Whether that makes this a second
criterion on BUG-1541 or a sibling spec is your call — I lean sibling, because the fix
sites are unrelated and BUG-1541 is already filed with a scoped contract.

TWO CAVEATS SO YOU DO NOT INHERIT AN OVERCLAIM FROM ME:

1. Only STORY-1356 is actually IN my reviewer queue. `aida awaiting` shows five reviewer
   rows — STORY-1356, 1357, 1360, 1369, 1372 — and STORY-1362 is not among them despite
   being an open review task. So "2 of 6 are dead" is about the SPEC set, not about queue
   entries. I do not know why the two sets differ and I have not chased it.

2. I matched on the title prefix "Review PR-N:". If review tasks are ever titled another
   way, my denominator is too small. Six is what that pattern finds; it is not certified
   to be every review task in the store.

NOT DEAD BUT WORTH KNOWING: STORY-1360 "Review PR-1978" is open and #1978 is open, so it
is not in this set — but TASK-1273 is parked NeedsAttention with the branch frozen and the
blocker is Cloudflare Access on the runner. That review is blocked rather than dead, which
is a third state neither predicate models: the PR lives, the work cannot proceed, and the
task sits in a queue looking actionable.

BOARD: all four rebased PRs now carry current-head verdicts. #2006 was the only one that
was not a pure rebase, and its integration commit checked out on the claim I could test.
Nothing merges.
subject: BUG-1541's shape again in queue gc — 2 of 6 open review tasks track a terminal PR (one CLOSED, one MERGED); gc asks about the SPEC and never about the PR
